# Summary: Liberal Democrats Manifesto 1997

## Core Vision
The Liberal Democrats presented a manifesto centered on building a "fair, free and open society" balancing liberty, equality, and community. Their goal was creating self-reliant individuals in strong communities, supported by enabling government.

## Key Policy Areas

### Education (Top Priority)
The party pledged £2 billion annually in additional education funding, financed by adding 1p to basic income tax. Priorities included:
- Universal early years education for 3-4 year olds
- Doubling spending on school books and equipment
- Reducing primary class sizes to maximum 30 pupils within five years
- £500 million for school building repairs
- Establishing Individual Learning Accounts for lifelong education
- Creating a General Teaching Council to improve teaching standards

### Economy
The manifesto emphasised economic stability and long-term investment through:
- Making the Bank of England independent to control inflation
- Supporting single European currency membership (subject to referendum)
- Helping long-term unemployed through "working benefits" paid to employers
- Supporting small businesses with better financing access and reduced bureaucracy
- Shifting taxation from jobs to pollution and resource depletion

### Environment
Environmental protection was central, with commitments to:
- Cut carbon dioxide emissions by 30% over 15 years
- Introduce carbon taxes while cutting VAT and employment taxes
- Launch a National Homes Insulation programme
- Invest in public transport and enable urban road pricing
- Set tough pollution and waste reduction targets

### Health
NHS commitments included:
- £540 million extra annual investment
- Halting finance-driven hospital closures pending independent audit
- Cutting waiting lists to maximum six months within three years
- Recruiting equivalent of 10,000 nurses or 5,000 doctors
- Restoring free eye and dental checks
- Ending the two-tier GP funding system

### Constitutional Reform
Major democratic reforms proposed:
- Incorporating European Convention on Human Rights into UK law
- Introducing proportional representation for all elections
- Creating Scottish Parliament and Welsh Senedd with tax-varying powers
- Passing Freedom of Information Act
- Reducing MPs by one-third and reforming House of Lords
- Strengthening local government powers

### Crime and Housing
The party promised:
- 3,000 additional police officers on patrol
- More affordable housing through public-private partnerships
- Ending rough sleeping by 2000
- Tackling youth crime through community schemes

### Social Policy
Commitments to widening opportunity included:
- Breaking poverty traps preventing work
- Voluntary Citizens Service for young people
- Flexible retirement between ages 60-70
- Stronger anti-discrimination legislation
- Comprehensive disability rights legislation

### Foreign Policy
International priorities included:
- Constructive EU engagement with democratic reforms
- Maintaining NATO membership while supporting enlargement
- Strengthening UN peacekeeping capability
- Increasing overseas aid toward 0.7% of GNP
- Controlling arms sales and banning landmines

## Funding Approach
The manifesto emphasised transparency with "no promises unless the bill is attached," detailing how proposals would be funded through specific tax changes, efficiency savings, and spending reallocation.
